Distribution and habitat notes. Known only from the type locality, a flooded area near the arroyo Crespo, belonging to Río San Martin drainage, a tributary of the Río Iténez, Río Madeira system, Amazon River basin, Bolivia (Fig. 5). At the time of collection of the type series, the type locality (Fig. 6) consisted in a flooded area, approximately 20 meters in diameter, and 0.1 to 0.2 meters deep, presenting muddy bottom with leaves and branches, brown, turbid still water with the following chemical-physical parameters (measured on late morning): conductivity: 7 µS, pH 5.6, and temperature 28 ° C. No other fish species were recorded.
Distribution. Only known in the type locality. Hosts. Uknown.

Distribution. Iliahia santalata appears to be primarily a low- to mid-elevation species on Oʻahu, as the highest elevation it has been recorded is ca. 500 meters. This roughly corresponds to the elevational distribution of the two native species of Santalum on Oʻahu, with no species occurring above ca. 800 m (Harbaugh et al. 2010). Five specimens of what appears to be this species are known from Kauaʻi (n = 1) and Hawaiʻi island (n = 4); additional surveys, ideally paired with DNA analysis, are needed to confirm the presence of I. santalata on these islands.
